raw_response:
*Settling in, thinking out loud as the old farmer...*

---

Well, I'm 65 now, been working this ground for 30 years. My boy helps sometimes but he works in town most of the year. Wife and I and my daughter-in-law handle most of it. 10.7 mu isn't much — three strips really, two on the good side near the well, one out back that dries out faster. Wheat then maize, wheat then maize, same as my father did.

**On wheat.** I'll plant around October 10th or so, same as always. Last year I waited till the 15th because it rained and couldn't get the tractor in, and the wheat came up weak going into winter — I don't want that again. I buy seed from the shop in the town, that Jimai variety most folks around here use. Old Wang next door tried some new variety two years back, paid extra, and his yield wasn't any better than mine, so I'm sticking with what I know. About 30 yuan a mu for seed, maybe a bit more.

For fertilizer I put down one bag of compound (the 15-15-15 kind, about 40 kg) per mu before I plow — that's what the agri-store sells and that's what everyone uses. Then at jointing time in March, if the wheat looks a little yellow, I broadcast about half a bag of urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. If it looks good and green, I use less. My neighbor's boy who went to agricultural school told me I'm using a bit much but I'd rather have too much than too little — one bad year and we're eating into savings.

Irrigation — I do the winter watering in late November before the ground freezes hard, then again at jointing, and once more at grain-filling if May is dry. Three times usually. The well is metered, costs me about 40 yuan each time per mu, so I don't do it more than I have to.

Hire the rotary tiller from old Li, 40 yuan a mu. Spray herbicide once in spring for the weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I spray once. That's it.

Expect maybe 450 kg per mu if the weather's decent. Got 480 two years ago, 400 last year because of that late frost.

**On maize.** The day after wheat harvest in early June I get right on it — no time to waste, if you plant after June 20th the yield drops. Buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that's similar, about 50 yuan a mu. I don't plow between wheat and maize, just no-till seed straight in — I hire a seeder for 30 yuan a mu, done in half a day.

Fertilizer for maize: another bag of compound at planting in the furrow, then urea at knee-high, maybe 20 kg per mu. If the summer rain comes I don't irrigate much, maybe once after planting to make sure it germinates. If July is dry I'll irrigate once at tasseling, that's when it really matters.

Herbicide after planting, and I watch for armyworm and corn borer — spray once if I see damage.

Expect 480 kg per mu. Maize has been more reliable than wheat for me the last few years.

**On money.** I've got maybe 4,500 yuan set aside for inputs this year. That's tight. Family does the planting, weeding, and most of the harvest ourselves — only hire help for wheat harvest because it all has to come off fast before the maize goes in. My grandson might help in summer when school's out.
